method: Complete named explanatory fields from the exact subject/pointer. Original summaries, subjects and historical reviews unchanged. This is an excerpt, not a standalone replacement contract or review.

summary.answer: The reset connection is a conditional cross-phase replacement, not an atomic respawn cleanup. It disables offhands and sets a reset flag before a native-use wait; early return or receiver cancellation can bypass its clear/reenable tail. A normal path requests item removal, optionally calls the current loadout pointer, replaces inventory with31 blank slots and dispatches inventory_reset after clearing its flag. It does not join older health/debit/removal threads or directly clear all health readiness fields. Spawn only conditionally initializes missing inventory in its own callback, and the world flag barrier is not a child-thread join. Old captured numeric IDs and object references therefore retain explicit cross-reset identity/scheduling gaps. All claims are bounded recovered-source drafts; original HMH build/settings/native behavior remains unproved.
unknowns: No guaranteed cleanup after early return, death/disconnect termination, opaque pointer failure or a nonterminating native-use wait. External cleanup is neither proved nor excluded.
No generation-token guarantee or original network-ID uniqueness/recycling proof across inventory replacement; previous references may outlive the receiver-field assignment under unknown VM semantics.
Reset/init directly leave the separately named busy and type23 markers alone in cited spans. Native callbacks or other source paths may clear them; global absence is not claimed.
The world barrier has independent player snapshots, alive/defined filters and no explicit reset-thread join. Original scheduler interleaving and actual HMH route selection remain open.
